Answer: B
Reason: Scimitar syndrome is characterized by partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (scimitar vein) from the right lung to the IVC, accompanied by right lung hypoplasia and dextroposition of the heart. Option B correctly identifies the key associated findings of right-sided opacity (hypoplasia) and dextroposition, whereas other options describe unrelated pathologies or incorrect anatomy (e.g., drainage into SVC).
